notes:
Summary: Enterprise procurement for Private VPC deployment. Primary concerns: HIPAA/BAA for PHI, SOC2/ISO evidence for vendor management, PCI scope reduction for payment flows, KMS/customer-managed keys, audit logging and retention, and strict data residency (US-only).

Compliance mapping (high-level):
- SOC 2: Redwood Private VPC maps to logical and physical access controls (CC6), system operations (CC7), and change management (CC8). We emphasized: RBAC, SSO/SAML integration, tenant isolation via VPC, and audit logging export. Customer asked for SOC2 Type II statement and subcontractor SOC2 reports for infra components.
- ISO 27001: Controls around A.9 (access control), A.12 (operations), A.13 (communications security) align with our Private offering. Need to provide statement of applicability and evidence for patching/SCM practices on private control plane.
- HIPAA / BAA: Customer requires a signed BAA. Key points: PHI must not be logged to shared telemetry; option to disable analytics for their tenancy; encryption at rest (customer-managed keys) and in transit mandatory. Discussed proof points: encryption algorithms, KMS integration flow, key rotation policy, and audit trails for key usage. Legal requested sample BAA + appendix on data flows.
- PCI considerations: Payments processing brings PCI scope. Suggested approaches: minimize cardholder data touching Redwood by using client-side tokenization, PCI-scope isolation inside VPC, strict logging redaction, and network segmentation. They will consult their QSA; asked for architecture diagram showing MAD (merchant acceptance device) boundary and Redwood's control points.

Technical specifics / asks from customer:
- KMS: Customer wants CMK from AWS KMS (shared via external key policy) or HSM-backed keys. POC to demonstrate decrypt only inside dedicated infra; request API for key rotation events.
- Audit logging: Must forward detailed audit logs (auth events, admin actions, model/version changes, infra events) to their Splunk/SIEM via secure forwarder. Retention controls adjustable per tenancy (90/365/730 days).
- Data residency: All data stored and processed in us-east-1/us-west-2 only. No cross-region fallbacks without explicit approval.
- Network: Private peering / AWS PrivateLink preferred. Egress NAT rules strict; need list of required outbound endpoints for updates/telemetry. IT team wants to run an on-prem firewall rule review.
- Pen testing & attestations: Customer asks about frequency of third-party pen tests and whether Redwood will allow truncated test in staging environment. Also asked if we have ISO 27001 certificate and scope details.
